findings.title: The tree's only ruleset reader never reads main-protect (deletion, non-fast-forward) or the release-tag ruleset
findings.claim: tools/policy/counts.mjs:liveRequiredContexts fetches only rulesets that contribute a required_status_checks rule, so 1 of the repository's 3 active rulesets is compared with its record: dropping main-protect 22628467's deletion and non_fast_forward rules, adding an always-bypass actor to it, disabling it, or emptying release-tags-protect 23937752 each leaves requiredContextsDrift at 0 errors, while the same class of edit on 23698884 yields 1-7.
findings.mechanism: The reader builds `ids` from branch rules filtered to type required_status_checks (counts.mjs, the `if (r.type !== 'required_status_checks') continue` line precedes `ids.add`), and requiredContextsDrift compares only the fetched objects; tools/ci/ruleset_cutover.py pins RULESET_ID = 23698884 alone. No other tracked script reads 22628467 or 23937752. The fixture's _comment records the choice: 22628467 is described there ('carries deletion and non-fast-forward') but deliberately left out of `rulesets`, so its rules are stated and never compared. Live re-read 2026-11-16 20:3x: 22628467's rules equal the capture.

findings.title: policy_lint --hooks accepts a wired hook neutered to `exit 0`: it reads the self-test's exit status, never its tally
findings.claim: Inserting `exit 0` as line 2 of any of the four hooks .claude/settings.json wires (pre-bash, pre-edit, session-start, stop-selfcheck) makes the hook refuse nothing and its --self-test print nothing, yet tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs:cmdHooks reports it `ok` and prints `HOOKS ok: 4 wired hook(s) exist and pass their own --self-test` (4 of 4 neutered arms accepted), while gutting only the hook's refusal exit is refused (3 of 3).
findings.mechanism: cmdHooks sets `verdict: code === 0 ? 'ok' : 'SELF-TEST FAILED'` from execFileSync('bash', [script, '--self-test']) and only prints the output's last line as `why`; an empty self-test exits 0. Every wired hook's self-test ends `printf '\n%s passed, %s failed\n'`, so the tally is available and unread. governance.yml (policy-docs) and prepr.sh's `hooks` step both run this check; it is the only CI read of the hooks.

evidence.unit: neutered hooks (of 4 wired) cmdHooks reports ok (gap_noop_accepted); control_refused=3 of 3, null_ok=4
evidence.contention_note: fan-out, other seats running; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: cmdHooks: `verdict: code === 0 ? 'ok'` -> `verdict: code === 0 && /^[1-9]\d* passed, 0 failed$/.test(tail) ? 'ok'` (harness --perturb, in a private worktree)

findings.metric_definition: Count of wired hooks whose `exit 0`-neutered copy policy_lint.mjs --hooks reports with verdict `ok`.
findings.phenomenon_property: A hook passes the hooks check only when its self-test demonstrably ran cases (a non-zero passed count and zero failed), so a hook that refuses nothing cannot read as wired and tested.

null_control.note: the controls show cmdHooks alive on a hook whose self-test runs and fails; only the self-test that runs nothing passes. Driven by hand too: `sed -i '1a exit 0' .claude/hooks/pre-bash.sh; node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs --hooks` in a worktree printed `ok ... pre-bash.sh` with an empty why and rc=0.

findings.title: prepr.sh --self-test never drives main-flow step 5: `no version edit` wired to 0 still gives 553 passed, 0 failed
findings.claim: Replacing the main flow's `step "no version edit" $? "$STAMPED"` in tools/pr/prepr.sh with `step "no version edit" 0 "$STAMPED"` (prepr then reports ok on a branch that moves VERSION, the manifest version or a notes heading) leaves tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test at 553 passed, 0 failed, identical to the unedited null arm, while gutting the version_edit() function it calls kills 9 cases.
findings.mechanism: The self-test drives version_edit() through `ve`/`veco` and the `--version-edit` entry point pr-contract runs (exiting before the main flow), but no case runs the main flow over a VERSION-moving branch and reads step 5's verdict; the step's own comment calls it the cheaper detector for the same refusal, so its wiring has no live control. The refusal still exists later (pr-contract's --version-edit, the pre-edit hook, the stamp), which bounds the consequence to a slower detection.

evidence.unit: self-test failures under step5_wiring_gutted (null 0; version_edit_gutted 9); mutants_killed=1 of 2

findings.proposed_fix_scope: tools/pr/prepr.sh --self-test: one end-to-end case running the main flow (PREPR_SKIP_CODE, a throwaway repo whose branch moves VERSION) and asserting `REFUSE no version edit`; then the other 23 step call sites measured by the same mutant (seam_rule). Mechanisation (D11.M5): a generic `step` wiring mutant lane, as policy_lint_mutants.mjs does for policy_lint, costs one script and about one self-test run per call site (about 15-25 min each here, provisional), so it fits a nightly lane, not a per-merge one.
